sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Essex County
sections.html:
Essex County has 22 municipalities, and each one has its own assessor and tax collector. The Essex County Board of Taxation sits above them at 495 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd., Room 230, in Newark. Its phone is 973-395-8525 and its website is essexcountynjtaxboard.org, where you will find appeal forms, tax rates, the equalization table, deduction forms and a contact list for every town's assessor and collector.

Bills combine school, municipal and county levies, so two similar houses in different Essex towns can land with quite different totals. The board posts pie charts showing how each town's tax dollar is divided, which is a quick way to see where your own money goes.

  • Assessor: sets the assessed value and handles deductions and exemptions.
  • Collector: mails the bill, receives payments and gives payoff figures.
  • County Tax Board: hears appeals and sets the tax rates each year.

sections.h2: Essex County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Essex County is crowded: about 896,000 people on 126.09 square miles of land, with Newark as the county seat. Typical home value for 2020 to 2024 is $524,100, and median gross rent is $1,531. Only 44.9% of households own their home, so renters fill most of the housing and many sales involve a tenant already in place. If you are selling a rented house, plan the showing schedule and any lease questions before you list.

The east side is anchored by Newark Liberty International Airport, Port Newark and Newark Penn Station. The west side holds the Oranges, Montclair, Verona and the Caldwells. Prices and tax bills vary a lot from one end of the county to the other, so use your own town's numbers rather than a county average.

Essex County follows the state calendar. The county board must have your petition in hand on April 1, or by the 45th day after the town finishes mailing assessment notices, whichever is later. Where a town has completed a municipal-wide revaluation or reassessment, the deadline is May 1. A postmark earns nothing here, and a late petition is thrown out.

If April 1 or May 1 falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, the last day moves to the following working day. Owners of property assessed above $1,000,000 may skip the county board and file in the Tax Court of New Jersey, with the same dates. The board's public schedule of meetings and tax appeal hearings is on its website.

sections.h2: How to file an Essex County appeal
sections.html:
Start with the state's Form A-1 and its comparable sales sheet, and file the original with the Essex County Tax Board. The board's site lists its current appeal forms and reminders, and the Division of Taxation has the same forms.

  • Build your case on market value as of October 1 of the pretax year. The appeal covers the assessed value alone.
  • List up to five comparable sales, giving block, lot, price and deed date for each. The board will not take other homes' assessments as comparables.
  • Check your town's average ratio on the equalization table. If the ratio of assessed to true value falls outside a band of 15 percent around the average, the board adjusts the value using that average ratio.
  • Serve a copy on your municipal assessor and clerk.
  • Attend the hearing yourself or send an attorney, unless you chose a summary hearing on written evidence.

If the board turns you down, the Tax Court in Trenton takes a complaint filed within 45 days of the judgment. A board judgment holds for the year and the two after it unless a revaluation or added assessment changes the picture.

sections.h2: What happens at a tax board hearing?
sections.html:
You pick the format on the petition: an in-person hearing, a virtual hearing if the county offers one, or a summary hearing decided only on the papers you send. A summary hearing means you cannot explain your comparables aloud, so every sale you rely on has to be clearly like your house. Homeowners may speak for themselves, while an LLC, trust or corporation needs a New Jersey attorney unless the property's prior-year tax was under $25,000.

The filing fee depends on assessed value. You pay by check to the County Tax Administrator, and the fee is not refundable.

Assessed valueFiling fee
Under $150,000$5
Up to $500,000$25

  • Adjournments are granted only for extraordinary reasons.
  • The town may cross-appeal, and you will be told and invited to attend.
  • If you rely on an appraisal, the appraiser has to appear and the report goes to the board at least seven days before the hearing.

Essex owners pay in four quarterly installments, due February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Many towns give a 10-day grace window after each date. Pay after that window and interest runs back to the original due date: 8 percent on the first $1,500 owed, then 18 percent on anything above. A delinquency over $10,000 left open at year end can also draw a penalty of up to 6 percent.

Towns run their own tax sales on the state framework, and a town lien blocks the sale of the house until it is redeemed. The collector can quote the exact payoff, and a title company will want it before closing.

Nothing stops you from selling a house that still has tax owing. The back tax, interest and any lien get paid out of your proceeds at closing, so get the figures early.

  • Get a payoff letter from the collector that states the daily interest.
  • Confirm whether the water or sewer account is separate from the tax account.
  • Pay the installment that falls during your closing window, or make sure the title company withholds it.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but the tax payoff still has to be settled before the deed is recorded, so the collector's letter matters just as much.

The state's fiscal year 2027 budget pays for Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ. Application windows run on a yearly cycle, so check the Division of Taxation page for the next one. The municipal assessor handles the $250 deductions for qualified veteran, senior and disabled owners, and the full exemption for a 100 percent disabled veteran. The Essex board lists those forms online.

Your status on October 1 of the year before the tax year decides eligibility, and the senior and disabled deduction carries an income ceiling of $10,000 that leaves out certain Social Security and pension income. If a town denies a deduction, you can appeal that denial to the county board without paying a filing fee. If you are selling, ask the assessor how a deduction on the house is handled once the deed changes hands.

faqs.q: Where do I send an Essex County property tax appeal?
faqs.a: Send it to the Essex County Board of Taxation, 495 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd., Room 230, Newark, NJ 07102. Call 973-395-8525 to check the hearing schedule and filing method.

faqs.q: What if my town just had a revaluation?
faqs.a: The deadline moves from April 1 to May 1 for that year. The board and your municipal assessor can confirm whether your town qualifies.

faqs.q: Is a late Essex County appeal ever accepted?
faqs.a: No. The petition has to be received by the end of business on the deadline date, and the board dismisses late filings.

faqs.q: Do I keep paying tax while an appeal is open?
faqs.a: Yes. You must stay current through the first quarter at least, and the board may relax that rule when justice requires.

faqs.q: Can an Essex County house sell with tax still owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and any lien are cleared from the seller's money at the table, so request a payoff letter from the municipal collector first.
